gen-gf-oxanium-gf-tiny5: Oxanium draws every stroke in one unbroken line, like bent wire. Tiny5 sits beneath it in sans-serif, tall in the body with ascenders that barely rise, so the two feel stacked rather than matched.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-truculenta: Truculenta packs its sans-serif letters into a tight, compact line with rounded shapes that stay open at the sides. Oxanium above it is bolder and more angular, while Truculenta keeps a longer read feeling snug and friendly.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-ubuntu: Strokes that look cut from sheet metal with a laser, all one width, give Oxanium its character in the heading. Ubuntu keeps a lofty lowercase band below, modern and sturdy.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-victor-mono: Precise and structured, Victor Mono leaves its monospace bowls open on one side and spaces its glyphs loosely, so text looks magnified. Oxanium's monoline heading gives it a commanding partner.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-viga: Viga reads as a plain sans with hairline-free, shadow-free strokes and capitals that barely rise above the lowercase. Oxanium's tall lowercase heading sits over it with more swagger.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-voces: Marker-drawn and bold. Voces follows in sans-serif with a tall lowercase and gently modulated strokes that never go harsh, which makes Oxanium's single-width letters feel like a sharper, more mechanical cousin.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-winky-rough: Tubing bent into letters, with a big lowercase. Winky Rough follows in sans-serif with a body height nearly matching its capitals, so a longer read feels dense and contemporary.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-winky-sans: Rounded-nib strokes with no swelling at the ends define Oxanium. Winky Sans, a modern sans with capitals barely taller than lowercase, would look flat if the heading shrank to its size.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-yantramanav: Oxanium has no hairlines at all, so its stems match every thin stroke. Yantramanav follows with a plain sans huddle of tall lowercase letters and spacious terminal gaps, which keeps a longer read clean and modern.
gen-gf-oxanium-outfit: Outfit reads like cable bent into shapes, with curves that finish well before they close and no swelling or thinning. Oxanium's higher lowercase gives the headline a more commanding stance.
